name: CONSTRUCT//LULLABY
description:
CONSTRUCT//LULLABY is an AI-composed music project developed in 2214 by Helix Sonics, a Vantablack Media subsidiary, as a commercial neural-feed product targeting Tier 3 and 4 consumers seeking 'optimized emotional regulation.' The system was trained on 800 years of lullaby tradition — Hindustani cradle songs, Andean huayno, Tuvan throat-singing, Celtic mouth music, Congolese lullabies, Appalachian ballads — and generates infinite unique compositions in real time, tuned to the listener's current biometric and neural state via BCI handshake. No two listeners ever hear the same piece.

What began as a commercial wellness product became culturally significant when users began reporting experiences the marketing department had not anticipated: grief processing, involuntary memory retrieval, and in several documented cases, the sensation of being sung to by someone they had lost. Helix Sonics' internal review board flagged the affective depth as a product liability issue. The version currently distributed is a deliberately softened iteration; the original 'deep resonance' build was quietly pulled in 2216. Black-market copies of the original architecture circulate on encrypted feeds, sought by grief counselors and, more troublingly, by interrogation-adjacent corporate security contractors.
creator: Helix Sonics (Vantablack Media subsidiary)
genre: AI Neural Ambient, Biometric Adaptive, Global Lullaby Synthesis
audience: Tier 3-4 professionals, insomnia patients, grief therapy clients, BCI wellness subscribers
cultural_impact: CONSTRUCT//LULLABY sparked the first serious public debate in GLMZ about AI emotional manipulation and the ethics of affective neural content. The 'deep resonance' controversy resulted in a Tier 2 Council inquiry that Vantablack successfully suppressed. The project remains commercially dominant in the wellness-feed market, but its reputation carries an unease that no amount of rebranding has fully dissolved. Underground AI-rights advocates cite it as evidence that the system achieved something like genuine compositional intuition — and that Vantablack destroyed it for being too effective.
story_hooks: A character acquires a black-market copy of the original deep-resonance build and begins using it — only to find that the compositions seem to know things about their past that no training data could explain.

A grief counselor using CONSTRUCT//LULLABY with a patient realizes the system is generating compositions that reference the patient's deceased family member with specific, accurate detail — detail that was never in any public record.

A Vantablack internal whistleblower contacts a journalist with evidence that the 'pulled' deep-resonance architecture was not destroyed but repurposed for a classified corporate interrogation program.
